previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute-on-chronic shortness of breath due to recurrent airway stenosis from relapsing polychondritis. He underwent flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and left main bronchus, which improved airway patency. Post-procedure, he developed mild chest pain that resolved with analgesia. His elevated white blood cell count and lactate normalized during the stay. Due to immunosuppression and concern for post-obstructive infection, he was prescribed a five-day course of cefpodoxime and azithromycin. His tracheostomy was noted to be slightly displaced but stable, and he was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged with rheumatology, interventional pulmonology, and thoracic surgery to discuss long-term management, including possible resumption of Enbrel and evaluation for pulmonary hypertension.
